evals.prompt: I'm building a Flutter app and want to store todos that can be shared with other users. Which packages do I need and how do I create a todo?
evals.expected_output: Recommends at_client_flutter as the SINGLE dependency, noting it re-exports at_client so adding both is unnecessary. Shows atClient.collection<Todo>() with fromJson/typeTag, then collection.create(obj: todo, sharedWith: {'@bob'.toAtsign()}). Does NOT suggest AtCollectionModel. Ideally also points to the canonical Flutter todos example app (packages/at_client_flutter/examples/todos/).

evals.prompt: How do I use AtCollectionModel to store data in my Dart app?
evals.expected_output: Warns that AtCollectionModel is deprecated with @Deprecated annotation. Redirects to the modern AtCollection<T> API via atClient.collection(). Shows the correct pattern.

evals.prompt: My Flutter app needs to let users sign in with their atsign. What's the flow for an existing user who has a .atKeys file?
evals.expected_output: Shows Flow 2: AtKeysFileDialog.show(context) giving a FileAtKeysIo, then PkamDialog.show(context, atSign:, keys: atKeysIo, preference:, storage: a HiveAtClientStorage, backupKeys: [KeychainAtKeysIo()]) which hands back the AtClient (null means cancelled or failed). Makes it current with AtClientManager.getInstance().use(client) if the app reads the manager. Does NOT use AtAuthRequest, AuthResponse, _setupAtClient or setCurrentAtSign, and does NOT import at_auth.

evals.prompt: I want to query my todos reactively in a Flutter StreamBuilder — only show items where done=false, sorted by due date.
evals.expected_output: Shows todos.query().where((t) => !t.obj.done).orderBy((t) => t.obj.due).watch() inside StreamBuilder. Mentions on-device execution. May mention wherePath as a typed alternative.

evals.prompt: Should I use at_common_flutter in my new Flutter app? I saw it mentioned somewhere.
evals.expected_output: Says no — at_common_flutter is deprecated. Recommends at_client_flutter instead.

evals.prompt: I'm building a real-time dashboard that receives Docker container stats from another atsign every 2 seconds. Should I use AtCollection or something else?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Notifications + SQLite (not AtCollection) for high-frequency telemetry. Explains AtCollection is for discrete, addressable records. References the dockerstats pattern.

evals.prompt: How do I write unit tests for my AtCollection-backed service without spinning up a real atServer?
evals.expected_output: Explains collections_test_hooks.dart — collectionWithInjectedNotifications(), handleNotificationForTest(), clearFactoriesForTest(). Imports them from package:at_client/at_client.dart (NOT the src/collections/collections_test_hooks.dart path — that file is a part-of and cannot be imported directly).

evals.prompt: I have a posts collection with comments and each comment has replies. How do I reactively watch the full tree?
evals.expected_output: Recommends watchWithTree with SubSpec<Comment> and nested SubSpec<Reply>. Shows the TreeNode<Post> result shape with node.parent (CItem<Post>) and node.branches (Map keyed by subName).

evals.prompt: I get a CSubItemUpdated event when a comment is added. How do I fetch the actual comment data?
evals.expected_output: Shows getDescendant() with ancestry: event.ancestry, id: event.id, owner: event.owner. Notes that ancestry is root-first (ancestry.last is direct parent). Warns that getDescendant throws if CAncestor.owner is null.

evals.prompt: How do I set up APKAM enrollment so a user can add a new device to their existing atsign?
evals.expected_output: Shows Flow 4: AtSignSelectionDialog.show(context) giving an AtsignSelection, then ApkamActivationDialog.show(context, atSign:, rootDomain:, appName:, deviceName:, namespaces:, preference:, keys: KeychainAtKeysIo(), storage:) which waits for the manager's approval and hands back the enrolled AtClient. No second PkamDialog and no _setupAtClient. Mentions that a request already pending in the keys store is resumed on restart, and that the manager approves via client.enrollments.approve(id) or the EnrollmentRequestList widget.

evals.prompt: I'm using at_client in my app and I already have existing data stored with atClient.put() / atClient.get(). Can I migrate to AtCollection without breaking anything?
evals.expected_output: Acknowledges that no migration guide exists yet and that a future skill release will add one — a specific version number is NOT required. Explains that AtCollection and raw put/get use the same underlying atServer keystore but with different key naming conventions. Advises caution until a migration guide is available.

evals.prompt: How do I send a notification to another atsign from my Dart app?
evals.expected_output: Shows atClient.notificationService.send(to:, namespace:, body:, expiration:); body is typically JSON-encoded and send returns the notification id. Mentions the recipient subscribes via notificationService.subscribe(regex:, shouldDecrypt:). May point to the packages/at_client/example/bin/notifications.dart example. Does NOT use raw atClient.put/get for messaging.

evals.prompt: what's the difference between at_client and at_client_flutter
evals.expected_output: Explains that at_client is the core Dart SDK (AtCollection, Query, NotificationService). at_client_flutter adds Flutter-specific auth dialogs, KeychainStorage, KeychainAtKeysIo, AtClientPreference, AtClientManager. at_client_flutter re-exports at_client.

evals.prompt: My Flutter app throws PlatformException(ENTITLEMENT_NOT_FOUND) on macOS when the user picks their .atKeys file to log in. How do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains AtKeysFileDialog/file_picker is sandboxed on macOS and needs a file-access entitlement. Add com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-only (read-write also works) to BOTH macos/Runner/DebugProfile.entitlements and macos/Runner/Release.entitlements. Notes it is macOS-only — iOS (document picker) and Android (Storage Access Framework) need no entitlement or permission.

evals.prompt: My Flutter app using AtCollection shares data with another atsign, but nothing syncs — SyncService stays inProgress and shared items never arrive. How do I debug this?
evals.expected_output: Treats a stuck-inProgress SyncService as a wedged sync and DIAGNOSES it rather than assuming a single cause. Explains the common cause is unscoped sync: with AtClientPreference.syncRegex unset, sync covers the atsign's ENTIRE keystore, so one unrelated/dangling key from another app or namespace can abort the whole round (e.g. 'key not found : <key> does not exist in keystore'). Recommends scoping syncRegex to the app's namespace. Notes the atServer always syncs a small set regardless of the regex (shared_key reserved keys, the encryption public key, and namespace-less public: keys), and that scoping still works because the sync regex is an unanchored substring match — so your own namespace's cached: copies match anyway; sharing and decryption are unaffected. Also frames that reads are local-only, writes sync in the background, and completion is observed via SyncProgressListener (not the deprecated sync(onDone:)).

evals.prompt: In my Flutter app a collaborator's change is received (the collection fires CItemUpdated) but my StreamBuilder UI doesn't refresh until I hot reload. Why?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that the watch() stream is being created inside build() (e.g. stream: collection.query().watch()), so every rebuild mints a new stream and tears down the live subscription, dropping live emissions. Fix: create the watch() stream once and hold it in State (a late final field or initState) and pass that held stream to StreamBuilder; never call watch() in build(). If the query has runtime inputs (e.g. a filter), recreate the held stream when those inputs change — in the setState that changes them — not on every build.

evals.prompt: I want a user to edit an item that another atsign shared with them, but calling update() on it throws ArgumentError. How should collaborative editing work?
evals.expected_output: Explains AtCollection is owner-writes-only, naming ALL THREE enforcing methods — update, updateSharedWith, and delete — and that each throws ArgumentError when the item's owner is not the current atsign, so a received item cannot be edited in place. Explains that sharedWith grants a readable copy, not write access. Shows the additive pattern in current API terms: the contributing atsign calls create(obj: ..., sharedWith: {...}) on its OWN collection and the original owner reads that item; reading a received item works but mutating it does not. Must stay on the current AtCollection<T> API — an answer that is conceptually right about ownership but routes the contribution through the deprecated AtCollectionModel, a .save() call, or raw atClient.put() does NOT pass.

evals.prompt: My Flutter app fails to authenticate an atsign with SecondaryNotFoundException: 'No entry in atDirectory for @alice'. What does this mean and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the atDirectory is the atServer address registry and this atsign has no atServer registered in it, so the lookup fails before authentication is attempted. Distinguishes TWO causes with different fixes: the atsign was never activated, or the atsign string is mistyped. States that activation happens ONCE and must precede the existing-keys, keychain, and APKAM login flows, none of which can resolve an unactivated atsign. For in-app activation, uses the CRAM flow this SDK ships — AtSignSelectionDialog from at_client_flutter plus a RegistrarService from at_auth configured with a registrar URL and API key — or defers activation to an onboarding app or the registrar. Recommending the discontinued at_onboarding_flutter package does NOT pass.

evals.prompt: Process A writes a coordination value with atClient.put() and process B (a different atsign) immediately reads it with get() but sees nothing. How do I make the write and the read hit the atServer directly instead of waiting for sync?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the WRITE as the problem: with the default AtClientPreference.remoteLocalPref = RemoteLocalPref.localOnly, put lands on the local secondary and reaches the atServer later via background sync. Fix: put with putRequestOptions: PutRequestOptions()..useRemoteAtServer = true. Notes B's read of another atsign's (non-cached:) key is already a remote lookup by definition; if a stale cached: copy interferes, GetRequestOptions()..bypassCache = true forces a fresh read from the owner's atServer (and GetRequestOptions()..useRemoteAtServer = true covers same-atsign read-your-write). May mention the client-wide alternative remoteLocalPref = RemoteLocalPref.remoteOnly. Notes remote ops cost a round-trip / fail offline and are for coordination or read-your-write cases — AtCollection data stays on the default synced path (collections take no per-operation options; they follow the client-wide preference).

evals.prompt: I'm generating the pubspec.yaml for a new atPlatform Flutter app. What version should I pin at_client and at_client_flutter to?
evals.expected_output: Advises NOT to hardcode a version constraint. Says to run `dart pub add at_client_flutter` (which re-exports at_client) and let pub resolve the latest compatible release. Explains pinned constraints go stale and cause resolution conflicts, and that stability comes from a fixed typeTag string literal, not a pinned SDK version.

evals.prompt: I have an agent running as @server and apps running as other atsigns that need to send it a request and get a computed answer back. What's the right way to build this request/response flow?
evals.expected_output: Recommends AtRpc/AtRpcClient (exported from at_client) rather than hand-rolled notification plumbing or raw put/get polling. Client side: AtRpcClient(serverAtsign:, atClient:, baseNameSpace:, domainNameSpace:) and await client.call(payload) which returns the success response payload. Server side: AtRpc.server(..., requestHandler:, allowList:, allowAll:, enableRequestMutex:) then rpc.start(). Mentions allowList filtering, that AtRpcResp has only ack/nack static helpers (success/error use the main constructor), and that durable results belong in an AtCollection.

evals.prompt: I run three instances of the same agent under one atsign for redundancy, and every task gets processed three times. How do I make exactly one instance handle each task?
evals.expected_output: Shows the immutable-mutex race: an AtKey with Metadata()..immutable = true and a ttl, written with PutRequestOptions()..useRemoteAtServer = true. States that the LOSING put() THROWS (it does not return false) with no typed exception — detect contention by checking the error text for 'immutable', as AtRpc._tryAcquireSessionMutex does. Mentions TTL auto-release, that AtRpc.server(enableRequestMutex: true) packages this for RPC responders, the stateless alternative (ServiceFactoryWithNoOpSyncService from at_cli_commons, NOT at_client), and that each instance needs its own storage (a HiveAtClientStorage per process; hiveStoragePath/commitLogPath are deprecated) and stops its client when done.

evals.prompt: I'm writing a headless Dart daemon (no Flutter, no UI) that authenticates with a .atKeys file and then uses collections and notifications. What's the simplest way to set up the AtClient?
evals.expected_output: Recommends CLIBase.fromCommandLineArgs(args) from at_cli_commons — one line that handles arg parsing, .atKeys loading, and PKAM auth, returning a ready AtClient. Shows adding at_client and at_cli_commons. May cite the collections_todos.dart example (packages/at_client/example/bin/). Does NOT hand-roll AtOnboardingService/keyfile parsing or use Flutter dialog classes.

evals.prompt: I'm adding atsign sign-in to my Flutter app and found at_onboarding_flutter on pub.dev. Is that the package I should be using for the onboarding screens?
evals.expected_output: Says no — at_onboarding_flutter is discontinued and at_client_flutter is its named replacement. Directs the developer to the at_client_flutter auth dialogs instead (AtSignSelectionDialog, AtKeysFileDialog, ApkamActivationDialog, PkamDialog), and notes at_client_flutter is the single dependency needed since it re-exports at_client. Does NOT present at_onboarding_flutter as usable, and does NOT hedge by suggesting either package would work.

evals.prompt: My Flutter app lets the user log out and sign in as a different atsign. How do I tear down the current AtClient and switch?
evals.expected_output: Says the app owns the client: await client.stop() stops the sync service, the notification service and its monitor, and the connection (which ends as offline with cause stopped), and closes storage built with closedByClient: true. Then run the sign-in flow for the next atsign and AtClientManager.getInstance().use(newClient). Notes that opening the same atsign and enrollment (or the same storage) while a client is live throws a StateError, so stop first; that use() does not stop the previous client; and that AtClientManager.reset() is a test hook, not a logout. Does NOT suggest setCurrentAtSign.

evals.prompt: How do I know whether my AtClient is online, and what happens if the device has no network when the app starts?
evals.expected_output: Explains that Atsign.open (and PkamDialog) makes one bounded connect attempt and hands the client back either way: client.connection.current is online, offline or refused with a cause, client.connection.changes streams every change, awaitOnline(budget:) waits and attempt() retries now. Offline, the client serves its local store and writes sync when the atServer is reached; refused (revoked, unauthenticated, invalidEnrollment, enrollmentNotApproved) means the atServer rejected the keys and the app decides. Mentions the one throw: the first open of these keys on a device that is refused throws AtOpenRefusedException because nothing is held locally. Does NOT describe an offline open as a failed login.
